about.title: Bell Gardens Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Bell Gardens residents rely daily on consumer goods, auto parts, appliances, and workplace equipment, and when one of those products fails, the injuries can be sudden and severe. California law generally does not require an injured person to prove the manufacturer was careless — under strict liability, showing the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused harm, is often enough. That matters in a dense, working-class city like Bell Gardens, where products move through busy commercial corridors, warehouses, and homes near Eastern Avenue and Garfield Avenue every day. If a faulty product hurt you or someone in your family, keeping the item itself, along with packaging, receipts, and any warnings, can matter later. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect Bell Gardens residents with independent attorneys who evaluate these claims for free and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Bell Gardens Families

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, showing the product itself was defective and caused your injury is often enough — you don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which matters when a defective product passed through several hands before reaching a Bell Gardens home or business.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on examining the defect, preserving the product, its packaging, and any instructions can matter for the attorney evaluating your case.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused injury, not on proving carelessness. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this may apply.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence can be important for an attorney evaluating a claim tied to a defect.
